<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="1m-token-context-window"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#1m-token-context-window">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">1M token context window</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 support the <a class="link" href="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows#context-window-sizes-by-model" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">1M token context window</a> on Amazon Bedrock. Sonnet 5 always runs with the 1M window on both the Invoke API and the <a class="link" href="#use-the-mantle-endpoint">Mantle endpoint</a>, with no <code>[1m]</code> variant to select. For the other models, Claude Code automatically enables the extended context window when you select a 1M model variant.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <a class="link" href="#sign-in-with-bedrock">setup wizard</a> offers a 1M context option when it pins models. To enable it for a manually pinned model instead, append <code>[1m]</code> to the model ID. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#pin-models-for-third-party-deployments">Pin models for third-party deployments</a> for details.</span>

<span data-as="p"><a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Amazon Bedrock Guardrails</a> let you implement content filtering for Claude Code. Enable Cross-Region inference on your Guardrail if you’re using cross-region inference profiles.</span>

<span data-as="p">Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API. It uses the same AWS credentials, IAM permissions, and <code>awsAuthRefresh</code> configuration described earlier on this page.</span>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code constructs the endpoint URL from the AWS region. As of v2.1.172, the region is resolved with the same precedence as <a class="link" href="#3-configure-claude-code">Amazon Bedrock above</a>; earlier versions use <code>AWS_REGION</code> only. To override the URL for a custom endpoint or gateway, set <code>ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Run <code>/status</code> inside Claude Code to confirm. The provider line shows <code>Amazon Bedrock (Mantle)</code> when Mantle is active.</span>

<span data-as="p">Mantle uses model IDs prefixed with <code>anthropic.</code> and without a version suffix, for example <code>anthropic.claude-sonnet-5</code> or <code>anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5</code>. The models available to your account depend on what your organization has been granted; additional model IDs are listed in your onboarding materials from AWS. Contact your AWS account team to request access to allowlisted models.</span>

<span data-as="p">The models available to you on Mantle may not include every model you use today. Setting both <code>CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK</code> and <code>CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE</code> lets Claude Code call both endpoints from the same session. Model IDs that match the Mantle format are routed to Mantle, and all other model IDs go to the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API.</span>

<span data-as="p">To surface a Mantle model in the <code>/model</code> picker, list its ID in <code>availableModels</code> in your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings">settings file</a>. This setting also restricts the picker to the listed entries. Listing <code>anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5</code> removes the bare <code>haiku</code> alias from the picker, so also list version prefixes or full IDs for the versions you want to keep selectable. The Mantle ID and the <code>haiku</code> alias resolve to the same model family, so the merge keeps only the more specific entry. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#merge-behavior">Merge behavior</a>:</span>

<span data-as="p">Entries with the <code>anthropic.</code> prefix are added as custom picker options and routed to Mantle. Replace <code>anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5</code> with the model ID your account has been granted. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#restrict-model-selection">Restrict model selection</a> for how <code>availableModels</code> interacts with other model settings.</span>
<span data-as="p">When both providers are active, <code>/status</code> shows <code>Amazon Bedrock + Amazon Bedrock (Mantle)</code>.</span>

<span data-as="p">If your organization routes model traffic through a centralized <a class="link" href="/docs/en/llm-gateway">LLM gateway</a> that injects AWS credentials server-side, disable client-side authentication so Claude Code sends requests without SigV4 signatures or <code>x-api-key</code> headers:</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="authentication-loop-with-sso-and-corporate-proxies"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#authentication-loop-with-sso-and-corporate-proxies">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Authentication loop with SSO and corporate proxies</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">If browser tabs spawn repeatedly when using AWS SSO, remove the <code>awsAuthRefresh</code> setting from your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings">settings file</a>. This can occur when corporate VPNs or TLS inspection proxies interrupt the SSO browser flow. Claude Code treats the interrupted connection as an authentication failure, re-runs <code>awsAuthRefresh</code>, and loops indefinitely.</span>
<span data-as="p">If your network environment interferes with automatic browser-based SSO flows, use <code>aws sso login</code> manually before starting Claude Code instead of relying on <code>awsAuthRefresh</code>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="region-issues"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#region-issues">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Region issues</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">If you encounter region issues:</span>
<ul>
<li>Check model availability: <code>aws bedrock list-inference-profiles --region your-region</code></li>
<li>Switch to a supported region: <code>export AWS_REGION=us-east-1</code></li>
<li>Consider using inference profiles for cross-region access</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">If you receive an error “on-demand throughput isn’t supported”:</span>
<ul>
<li>Specify the model as an <a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-profiles-support.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">inference profile</a> ID</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code uses the Amazon Bedrock <a class="link" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_InvokeModelWithResponseStream.html" rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">Invoke API</a> and does not support the Converse API.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="streaming-errors-behind-a-gateway-or-proxy"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#streaming-errors-behind-a-gateway-or-proxy">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Streaming errors behind a gateway or proxy</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">If streaming requests fail with an error that begins <code>Bedrock streaming response has content-type</code>, a gateway or proxy between Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock is transforming the streaming response. Amazon Bedrock streams responses in a binary event-stream format with the content-type <code>application/vnd.amazon.eventstream</code>, and Claude Code rejects a successful streaming response that reports a different content-type instead of decoding a body it can’t read. The error names the content-type it received, commonly <code>text/event-stream</code> from an Amazon API Gateway and Lambda integration that re-emits the stream as server-sent events.</span>
<span data-as="p">Before v2.1.208, the same misconfiguration surfaced as <code>API Error: Truncated event message received</code> after the whole response had been buffered.</span>
<span data-as="p">To fix it, configure the gateway to pass the <code>InvokeModelWithResponseStream</code> response body and its <code>Content-Type</code> header through unmodified. If the gateway rewrites only the header and passes the binary body through intact, set <a class="link" href="/docs/en/env-vars"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BEDROCK_CONTENT_TYPE_GUARD=1</code></a> to skip the check until the gateway is fixed. With the check off, a response body that was transformed fails with <code>Truncated event message received</code> again.</span>
<span data-as="p">When a successful streaming response arrives with a missing or empty <code>Content-Type</code> header, Claude Code decodes the body as the binary event-stream format. Amazon Bedrock always sends the header, so a missing header means an intermediary stripped it. If your proxy strips the header and also re-emits the body as server-sent events, set <a class="link" href="/docs/en/env-vars"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BEDROCK_CONTENT_TYPE_DEFAULT=1</code></a> so Claude Code reads the body as server-sent events instead.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="zero-token-counts-in-/context"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#zero-token-counts-in-/context">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Zero token counts in /context</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">The <code>/context</code> command counts tokens for each tool group by sending the tool schemas to the Amazon Bedrock count-tokens API. On Claude Code versions before v2.1.196, Amazon Bedrock rejected that request because the schemas carried fields its count-tokens API doesn’t accept, so every tool group showed 0 tokens. Other rows in the breakdown, such as messages and memory files, aren’t affected.</span>
<span data-as="p">Update to v2.1.196 or later.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="mantle-endpoint-errors"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#mantle-endpoint-errors">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Mantle endpoint errors</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">If <code>/status</code> does not show <code>Amazon Bedrock (Mantle)</code> after you set <code>CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE</code>, the variable is not reaching the process. Confirm it is exported in the shell where you launched <code>claude</code>, or set it in the <code>env</code> block of your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings">settings file</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">A <code>403</code> from the Mantle endpoint with valid credentials means your AWS account has not been granted access to the model you requested. Contact your AWS account team to request access.</span>
<span data-as="p">A <code>400</code> that names the model ID means that model is not served on Mantle. Mantle has its own model lineup separate from the standard Amazon Bedrock catalog, so inference profile IDs such as <code>us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6</code> will not work. Use a Mantle-format ID, or enable <a class="link" href="#run-mantle-alongside-the-invoke-api">both endpoints</a> so Claude Code routes each request to the endpoint where the model is available.</span>

resolves the AWS default credential provider chain once and keeps the resolved credentials in memory. It reuses them until five minutes before they expire, or for one hour when they carry no expiration, so an SSO-backed profile requests credentials from IAM Identity Center about once per credential lifetime. A credential error from the API clears the cache, and the retry resolves fresh credentials. Requires Claude Code v2.1.207 or later.`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`The cache covers every credential option above except an Amazon Bedrock API key, which doesn’t use the provider chain. To resolve the chain on every request instead, set `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/env-vars`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_AWS_CRED_CACHE=1`})}),`.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`Each resolve of the chain times out after 60 seconds. If your chain runs an interactive sign-in that legitimately needs longer, such as browser-based SSO with MFA through a wrapper like `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`aws-vault`}),`, raise the limit in milliseconds with `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/env-vars`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_AWS_CHAIN_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS`})}),`. Before v2.1.207, a stalled credential resolution left the request waiting indefinitely.`]}),`\n`,_jsx(Heading,{level:`4`,id:`advanced-credential-configuration`,children:`Advanced credential configuration`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`Claude Code supports automatic credential refresh for AWS SSO and corporate identity providers. fail with an error that begins `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Bedrock streaming response has content-type`}),`, a gateway or proxy between Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock is transforming the streaming response. Amazon Bedrock streams responses in a binary event-stream format with the content-type `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`application/vnd.amazon.eventstream`}),`, and Claude Code rejects a successful streaming response that reports a different content-type instead of decoding a body it can’t read. The error names the content-type it received, commonly `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`text/event-stream`}),` from an Amazon API Gateway and Lambda integration that re-emits the stream as server-sent events.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`Before v2.1.208, the same misconfiguration surfaced as `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`API Error: Truncated event message received`}),` after the whole response had been buffered.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`To fix it, configure the gateway to pass the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`InvokeModelWithResponseStream`}),` response body and its `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Content-Type`}),` header through unmodified. If the gateway rewrites only the header and passes the binary body through intact, set `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/env-vars`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BEDROCK_CONTENT_TYPE_GUARD=1`})}),` to skip the check until the gateway is fixed. With the check off, a response body that was transformed fails with `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Truncated event message received`}),` again.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`When a successful streaming response arrives with a missing or empty `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Content-Type`}),` header, Claude Code decodes the body as the binary event-stream format. If your proxy strips the header and also re-emits the body as server-sent events, set `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/env-vars`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BEDROCK_CONTENT_TYPE_DEFAULT=1`})}),` so Claude Code reads the body as server-sent events instead.`]}),`\n`,_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`zero-token-counts-in-/context`,children:`Zero token counts in /context`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`The `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`/context`}),` command counts tokens for each tool group by sending the tool schemas to the Amazon Bedrock count-tokens API. On Claude Code versions before v2.1.196, Amazon Bedrock rejected that request because the schemas carried fields its count-tokens API doesn’t accept, so every tool group showed 0 tokens. Other rows in the breakdown, such as messages and memory files, aren’t affected.`]}),`\n`,_jsx(_components.p,{children:`Update to v2.1.196 or later.`}),`\n`,_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`mantle-endpoint-errors`,children:`Mantle endpoint errors`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`If `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`/status`}),` does not show `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Amazon Bedrock (Mantle)`}),` after you set `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE`}),`, the variable is not reaching the process. resolves the AWS default credential provider chain once and keeps the resolved credentials in memory. It reuses them until five minutes before they expire, or for one hour when they carry no expiration, so an SSO-backed profile requests credentials from IAM Identity Center about once per credential lifetime. A credential error from the API clears the cache, and the retry resolves fresh credentials. Requires Claude Code v2.1.207 or later.`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`The cache covers every credential option above except an Amazon Bedrock API key, which doesn’t use the provider chain. To resolve the chain on every request instead, set `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/env-vars`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_AWS_CRED_CACHE=1`})}),`.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`Each resolve of the chain times out after 60 seconds. If a step in the chain stalls, for example a `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`credential_process`}),` helper that waits for input it can’t receive, the request fails with `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/errors#aws-default-chain-credential-resolve-timed-out`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`AWS default-chain credential resolve timed out`})}),`. If your chain runs an interactive sign-in that legitimately needs longer, such as browser-based SSO with MFA through a wrapper like `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`aws-vault`}),`, raise the limit in milliseconds with `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/env-vars`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_AWS_CHAIN_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS`})}),`. Before v2.1.207, a stalled credential resolution left the request waiting indefinitely.`]}),`\n`,_jsx(Heading,{level:`4`,id:`advanced-credential-configuration`,children:`Advanced credential configuration`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`Claude Code supports automatic credential refresh for AWS SSO and corporate identity providers. Use this when your Amazon Bedrock account requires cross-account credentials that differ from the ones the default provider chain would resolve.`]}),`\n`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`Before running the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`awsAuthRefresh`}),` command, Claude Code makes an STS `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`GetCallerIdentity`}),` call to confirm that your credentials are actually expired, and skips the command when they still work. a user selects one of these versions in `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`/model`}),`, Claude Code calls Amazon Bedrock with the mapped ARN. The same mapping applies when you pass the Anthropic model ID directly through `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`--model`}),` or `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`}),`. Versions without an override fall back to the built-in Amazon Bedrock model ID or any matching inference profile discovered at startup. Before v2.1.200, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`--model`}),` and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`}),` values reached Amazon Bedrock as-is without going through the override map. See `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/model-config#override-model-ids-per-version`,children:`Override model IDs per version`}),` for details on how overrides interact with `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`availableModels`}),` and other model settings.`]}),`\n`,_jsx(Heading,{level:`2`,id:`startup-model-checks`,children:`Startup model checks`}),`\n`,_jsx(_components.p,{children:`When Claude Code starts with Amazon Bedrock configured, it verifies that the models it intends to use are accessible in your account.`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`If you have pinned a model version that is older than the current Claude Code default, and your account can invoke the newer version, Claude Code prompts you to update the pin. Accepting writes the new model ID to your `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/settings`,children:`user settings file`}),` and restarts Claude Code. Declining is remembered until the next default version change. Pins that point to an `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`#map-each-model-version-to-an-inference-profile`,children:`application inference profile ARN`}),` are skipped, since those are managed by your administrator.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`If you have not pinned a model and the current default is unavailable in your account, Claude Code falls back for the current session and shows a notice. fail with an error that begins `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Bedrock streaming response has content-type`}),`, a gateway or proxy between Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock is transforming the streaming response. Amazon Bedrock streams responses in a binary event-stream format with the content-type `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`application/vnd.amazon.eventstream`}),`, and Claude Code rejects a successful streaming response that reports a different content-type instead of decoding a body it can’t read. The error names the content-type it received, commonly `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`text/event-stream`}),` from an Amazon API Gateway and Lambda integration that re-emits the stream as server-sent events.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`Before v2.1.208, the same misconfiguration surfaced as `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`API Error: Truncated event message received`}),` after the whole response had been buffered.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`To fix it, configure the gateway to pass the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`InvokeModelWithResponseStream`}),` response body and its `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Content-Type`}),` header through unmodified. If the gateway rewrites only the header and passes the binary body through intact, set `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/env-vars`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BEDROCK_CONTENT_TYPE_GUARD=1`})}),` to skip the check until the gateway is fixed. With the check off, a response body that was transformed fails with `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Truncated event message received`}),` again.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`When a successful streaming response arrives with a missing or empty `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Content-Type`}),` header, Claude Code decodes the body as the binary event-stream format. Amazon Bedrock always sends the header, so a missing header means an intermediary stripped it. If your proxy strips the header and also re-emits the body as server-sent events, set `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/en/env-vars`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BEDROCK_CONTENT_TYPE_DEFAULT=1`})}),` so Claude Code reads the body as server-sent events instead.`]}),`\n`,_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`zero-token-counts-in-/context`,children:`Zero token counts in /context`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`The `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`/context`}),` command counts tokens for each tool group by sending the tool schemas to the Amazon Bedrock count-tokens API. On Claude Code versions before v2.1.196, Amazon Bedrock rejected that request because the schemas carried fields its count-tokens API doesn’t accept, so every tool group showed 0 tokens. Other rows in the breakdown, such as messages and memory files, aren’t affected.`]}),`\n`,_jsx(_components.p,{children:`Update to v2.1.196 or later.`}),`\n`,_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`mantle-endpoint-errors`,children:`Mantle endpoint errors`}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[`If `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`/status`}),` does not show `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Amazon Bedrock (Mantle)`}),` after you set `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE`}),`, the variable is not reaching the process.
